# Acceptance E: cached stream and numerical coverage

| Contract | Evidence now | Remaining qualification |
|---|---|---|
| Batch sizes 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 | `test_action_sequence_kv_batch.py` compares each prepared bucket against independent CPU FP32 rows at Q1/2/4 and CUDA BF16 conditional logits through ring eviction. CUDA graph tests exercise B1/B2; the spawned-process benchmark delivers real B2 plans. | Full-path throughput and capacity at B4/8/16/32 on Ada hardware. The 32-admitted sparse run has only two ready rows. |
| Independent positions, wrap, reset, and row permutation | `test_action_sequence_kv_batch.py` uses unequal update histories, reversed/sparse rows, repeated ring wraps, one-row reset, and exact persistent cache comparisons. `test_action_sequence_kv_reference.py` covers Q1/2/4 against the uncached banded trunk. | Long-running production checkpoint soak. |
| Prefill, Q1/2/4, and decomposed counts | `test_action_sequence_prefill.py` checks parallel prefixes and draw count. `test_action_sequence_policy_batch.py` compares Q3 as 2+1 and counts 5/6/7 as prepared steps with no dummy time frames. | GPU stress at larger ready batches. |
| Fixed prefixes 0, 2, 3, 4 | `test_action_sequence_policy_batch.py` compares two ready rows with serial execution for every shape and target frame. Its mixed-profile test shares one model across H4/prefix0, H8/prefix3, and H8/prefix4, including captured CUDA execution with recompilation forbidden. | Real checkpoint profile-specific gameplay and timing gates. |
| Stream settings and sampling | Three ready CPU rows carry distinct player ranks, return targets including absent conditioning, and temperatures 0.8/1.0/1.1. Plans and exact RNG counters match serial rows through permutation and a dummy bucket row. `test_inference_sampling.py` covers sparse sets, joins/leaves, explicit generations, release, restore, and no tombstones. | CUDA BF16 sampled categories may differ near boundaries; distribution limits, not action bitwise equality, are the gate. |
| Sparse readiness, arbitrary IDs, release/reuse, rematches | CPU policy tests use arbitrary IDs, 32 admitted with two ready, row reuse, unchanged inactive cache/RNG, and stable prepared storage. CUDA graph tests confirm B1/B2 capture before arbitrary admission and reuse. Process benchmark confirms 32 admitted/two ready uses B2, not B32. | Service failure/restart and long match/rematch gates. |
| One weight copy and routing | `test_inference_engine.py` checks registry identity by checkpoint/device/dtype and rejects unsupported dtype. Mixed-profile tests share the same model object and independent cache pools. | Real same/different checkpoint model-versus-model route and Ada memory accounting. |
| FP32 numerical limits | Cache/model reference tests use `atol=2e-6, rtol=2e-5` for hidden/history. `test_fp32_batched_teacher_forced_decoder_logits_match_serial_after_eviction` uses `atol=2e-5, rtol=2e-4` through two ring wraps. | None for the tested proxy geometry; full checkpoint validation remains separate. |
| Production BF16 numerical limits | `production_bf16_kl.md`: 960 conditional distributions from the actual 246M checkpoint on the RTX 3060, before and after context eviction; mean KL `7.23e-5`, p99 `1.14e-3` nats against the old B1 streaming cache. | Extend to qualified Ada batch sizes/profiles. |

The CPU small-model matrix, 3060 B2 process result, and production checkpoint
KL are distinct controls. None substitutes for the Ada capacity or gameplay
qualification gates.

On the RTX 3060, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/hal-uv-cache uv run pytest -q tests/test_action_sequence_kv_batch.py -k cuda_bf16_batched_conditional_logits_match_serial_before_and_after_eviction -s` passed 6 batch sizes in 9.09 seconds. The small-model BF16 mean/p99 conditional KL values (n distributions) were B1 `0/0` (128), B2 `0/0` (256), B4 `0/0` (512), B8 `0/0` (1024), B16 `1.8153e-5/9.0610e-5` (2048), and B32 `1.8137e-5/8.1013e-5` (4096). Each run ingested eight Q4 updates against independent serial rows, crossing its context window. These are eager numerical tests on proxy geometry; the production-checkpoint B2 comparison and full-path process timings are reported separately.
